title: Minimum Operations to Make a Special Number
statement:
The string `num` holds the decimal digits of a non-negative integer. One operation erases a single digit of your choice; the digits that remain, read in their original order, form the new number, and erasing every digit leaves the number `0`.

Call a number special when it is a multiple of `25`. Return the smallest number of operations that leaves a special number.
constraints: num contains only the digits '0' to '9'
notes:
## Intuition

A number is a multiple of 25 exactly when it ends in `00`, `25`, `50` or `75`, or when it is `0` itself. Trying every subset of digits would be O(2ⁿ). Instead, pick the two digits that will become the new ending: if the first of them sits at index `i`, everything after `i` except the second one must be erased, which costs `n - i - 2`, and nothing before `i` needs to change. So the best pair is the one whose first digit lies furthest to the right, which a single right-to-left scan finds greedily.

## Approach

1. Scan `num` from the right, remembering whether a `0` (`seenZero`) or a `5` (`seenFive`) appeared to the right of the current index `i`.
2. If `digit` is `0` or `5` and a `0` lies to its right, the ending `00` or `50` is available: return `n - i - 2`.
3. If `digit` is `2` or `7` and a `5` lies to its right, the ending `25` or `75` is available: return `n - i - 2`.
4. Otherwise record whether `digit` is a `0` or a `5` and keep scanning.
5. With no pair, keep a lone `0` if there is one (`n - 1` erasures), or erase everything (`n`).

## Example 1, step by step

`num = "2245047"`, `n = 7`. At `i = 6` (`7`) and `i = 5` (`4`) nothing matches. At `i = 4` the digit `0` finds no zero to its right yet, so `seenZero` becomes true. At `i = 3` the digit `5` has a zero to its right, forming `50`, so the answer is `7 - 3 - 2 = 2` (erase the `4` and the `7`).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the digits.
- Space: O(1): two flags.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the fallback: a single `0` left alone is special, so the answer is `n - 1` when any zero exists.
- Erasing everything also gives `0`, so the answer never exceeds `n`.
- Update the flags after the pair checks, or a lone `0` would pair with itself as `00`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of digits |
| `i` | index of the candidate first digit of the ending |
| `digit` | the character `num[i]` |
| `seenZero` | a `0` exists to the right of `i` |
| `seenFive` | a `5` exists to the right of `i` |

narration.2: n is the number of digits we could erase.
narration.3: seenZero tells whether a 0 lies to the right of the current index.
narration.4: seenFive tells whether a 5 lies to the right of the current index.
narration.5: Scan from the right so the first pair found has its first digit as far right as possible.
narration.7: A 0 or 5 followed later by a 0 can end the number as 00 or 50.
narration.8: Keep this digit and that zero, erasing the other n - i - 2 digits after i.
narration.10: A 2 or 7 followed later by a 5 can end the number as 25 or 75.
narration.11: Same cost: everything after i except the chosen 5 is erased.
narration.13: Only now record this digit, so it never pairs with itself.
narration.16: Likewise remember a 5 for 2s and 7s further left.
narration.20: No ending pair exists: keep a lone 0 if there is one, otherwise erase every digit.
